text.p: Lithuania's Kalnapilis brewery said on Monday that its 1996 net profit had more than doubled to 10.4 million litas versus 4.2 million litas the previous year.
"Our profit in 1996 increased to 10.4 million litas from 4.2 million litas in 1995," the company's general director Lionginas Mackevichius told Reuters by phone from his office in Panevezhys.
He added that the company planned to pay dividends of 0.25 litas per share. The shares have a face value of one litas.
Mackevichius said that the company had 22 percent of the lucrative beer market in Lithuania but did not give a specific figure.
"We would like to increase our sales by one-third in 1997," he added.
The company, which is traded on the A list of the Vilnius bourse, is 86.3 percent foreign owned.
The major investors are Finland's Hartwell, Sweden's Pripps Ringness, and Norway's Orkla.
Mackevichius said that the company was only 50 percent exempt from profit tax because its foriegn capital did not exceed $2.0 million.
The company decided last month to boost its share capital to 25.3 million litas from 8.47 million litas.
